answer_1.quote: We further decompose abstractive QFS into two subtasks: (1) query modeling (i.e., finding supportive evidence within a set of documents for a query) and (2) conditional language modeling (i.e., generating an abstractive summary based on found evidence).

answer_2.quote: We use ROUGE as a distant supervision signal, and train a model that takes a query and document sentence as input and estimates their relevance.

answer_4.quote: We also evaluated model summaries in a judgment elicitation study via Amazon Mechanical Turk. Native English speakers (self-reported) were asked to rate query-summary pairs on two dimensions: Succinctness (does the summary avoid unnecessary detail and redundant information?) and Coherence (does the summary make logical sense?).
answer_4.guideline: Participants were asked to rate query-summary pairs on two dimensions: Succinctness and Coherence using a five-point Likert scale. For Relevance assessment, participants decided whether each sentence was relevant (score 5), partially relevant (score 2.5), or irrelevant (score 0).
